clue.text: Covert behaviour's appropriate, though heartless

parts.note: to appropriate something is to take it without permission, to steal it

indicators.note: the word though loses its middle letters, keeping only its two ends

explanation.surface: A sneaky act is justified, even if done without compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective meaning suitable, but here it is the verb to take. 'heartless' strips OUG from THOUGH, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is secretive, furtive conduct meant to go unnoticed, which is exactly covert behaviour.

clue.text: There's no end of unstable footwear

indicators.note: the synonym for unstable has its final letter cut off

parts.note: something unstable underfoot is slippery

explanation.surface: Wobbly shoes are always on offer, the clue seems to grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' looks like it means plenty, but it removes the last letter Y from SLIPPERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipper is a soft indoor shoe, one kind of footwear.

clue.text: Particularly reliable source of cash among sweetshop's stock?

parts.note: extra used as an intensifier means particularly, as in extra careful
a strong argument or person is sound and dependable
the mint is where coins and notes are made

explanation.surface: A very dependable money-maker found in a sweetshop's merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: Extra Strong Mints are a popular British brand of hard, powerful peppermint sweets. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: These peppermints are a staple confectionery item sold in British sweetshops.

clue.text: Vassal's superior, grand persona sent up in song

indicators.note: the grand letter and the upturned persona sit inside the word for song

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song
G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for persona is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a persona is a role one plays

explanation.surface: A feudal master is mocked in a ballad about his grandeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' suggests mockery, but in a down clue it means read upwards; 'in' puts the grand letter and the turned persona inside the German art song.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal society the lord to whom a vassal owed allegiance and service was his liege lord.

clue.text: Below-zero greeting?

parts.note: hell is traditionally the place below, the underworld
the figure zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A frosty welcome, perhaps one in freezing temperatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below-zero' reads as subzero cold, but splits into HELL (the place below) and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying hi is the commonest salutation, a standard word of greeting.

clue.text: Bail due for revision in hearing

indicators.note: letters put up for revision are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A court bail payment is being reconsidered at a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a court session, which the bail surface supports, but it means the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something within earshot can be heard, which is what being able to be perceived by the ear means.

clue.text: Distance from a kid climbing headland

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word reads upwards, back to front

parts.note: to kid someone is to fool them
a ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness's neighbour place names

explanation.surface: Keeping away from a youngster scrambling up a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb to fool, and FOOL climbs to LOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional reserve or detachment from others is a kind of distance, as in keeping one's distance.

clue.text: Bleak start for Doctor Foster

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word doctor is used

parts.note: to foster a child is to rear it

explanation.surface: A gloomy beginning for Doctor Foster, of the nursery rhyme who went to Gloucester in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Foster' looks like a single name from the British nursery rhyme, but the words work apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a literary form of dreary, meaning dismal and cheerless, so bleak.

clue.text: Like badly-synced dialogue offstage?

definitions.meaning: speech out of sync lags after the pictures, trailing the visuals on screen
out of sight of the audience, in the backstage area

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: dialogue running late lags after the scenes it belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means out of public view, where theatre crew work offstage.

clue.text: Set up a route regularly crossing one continent or two

definitions.text: Set up a route regularly crossing one continent or two

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the whole construction is read upwards
the pair of letters for one and the continent lie across the middle of the other pieces
every other letter of route is taken, starting with the first

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
SA is the abbreviation for South America, a continent

explanation.surface: Plan a journey that spans a continent or perhaps two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes alternate letters of route; 'crossing' puts one plus South America inside, making AISARUE, and 'Set up' reverses all of it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The landmass joining Europe and Asia can be counted as one continent or as two separate ones.

clue.text: Bare minimum of instructional books — effectively treat as one

indicators.note: the smallest part of the word instructional, its opening letter

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
to treat an illness effectively is to cure or heal it
acting as one means acting jointly, in unison

explanation.surface: The bare essentials of manuals, sensibly handled as a single unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bare minimum' reads as one phrase, but 'Bare' is the definition and 'minimum of' picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means stark naked, wearing nothing at all.

clue.text: Gifts of pink and yellow roses to make up?

definitions.text: Gifts of pink and yellow roses to make up?

parts.words: Gifts of pink and yellow roses to make up?
parts.note: A famous rose variety with pink-edged yellow blooms, so bunches given are its ..., and such presents are given to reconcile after a quarrel

explanation.walkthrough: Peace is a well-known hybrid tea rose, yellow flushed with pink; 'to make up' means to be reconciled.
explanation.definitionFit: Conciliatory gifts handed over after a falling-out, like flowers, are given to restore good relations.

clue.text: See 10
Reason address fails to start? One may be drunk

indicators.note: the synonym for address is missing its first letter

parts.note: a formal speech or address is an oration
ale is a beer, something one drinks

explanation.surface: A speaker cannot begin, perhaps because he has been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One may be drunk' looks like a person who is drunk, but it describes a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying logic or justification behind something, a reason.

clue.text: Favourite leader's lost weight where some US VIPs have gained stones

definitions.text: where some US VIPs have gained stones

indicators.note: the word for favourite drops its first letter

parts.note: a darling is a favourite person
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A dieting favourite has slimmed, while some American bigwigs have piled on the pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gained stones' suggests putting on weight (a stone is a British unit of 14 pounds), but means headstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia is where many prominent Americans are buried beneath headstones.

clue.text: Vestment about to be given extravagant lining

indicators.note: the extravagant letters line the inside of the abbreviation for about

parts.note: ca is short for circa, meaning about
OTT is short for over the top

explanation.surface: A church robe is about to get a lavish inner lining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to be' reads as soon to be, but 'about' is CA and 'to be given' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short surplice worn over a cassock, a church garment.

clue.text: Extremely little basis for appalling narrative

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters from little sit underneath, at the base

parts.note: chronic is informal British for very bad

indicators.note: only the extreme letters of little, its first and last

explanation.surface: There is hardly any foundation for a dreadful story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely little' reads as very little, but picks L and E, placed beneath CHRONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a factual account of events in order, a kind of narrative.

clue.text: Gathering clamour breaks record

indicators.note: the noise word breaks into the abbreviation for a record

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a recording
a row is a loud noise or din

explanation.surface: A noisy assembly sets a new record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks record' reads as setting a new best, but 'breaks' means the clamour splits the disc's abbreviation open.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd is a large group of people assembled together, a gathering.

clue.text: Slavonic firms on fire

parts.note: Cos is the plural abbreviation of company, so firms
to sack someone is to fire them

explanation.surface: Eastern European businesses go up in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on fire' reads as burning, but 'fire' means dismiss, and 'on' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks are a Slavic people of southern Russia and Ukraine, so the word describes something Slavonic.

clue.text: Powerful ray left sea bream floundering

indicators.note: struggling wildly, so the letters of the fish are thrashed about

explanation.surface: A strong ray, the fish, left a sea bream struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ray' and 'floundering' suggest fish, with a flounder pun, but the ray is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: An intense beam of focused light is a powerful ray.

clue.text: A rum old collection assembled bit by bit

indicators.note: a collection gathers items together into a fresh arrangement, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: An odd array of antiques built up piece by piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the anagram signal (it means odd), but it is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made of standard units fitted together is put together in sections, piece by piece.

clue.text: Glimpses tenor in embrace of lovelorn soprano

indicators.note: the tenor's letter is held inside the word for lovelorn

parts.note: a lovelorn person is sighing
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: An opera scene: the tenor clasps a pining soprano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embrace' paints an operatic clinch, but it puts T inside SIGHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Sightings are brief views of something, which is what glimpses are.

clue.text: Sufficient power to operate choppers

definitions.meaning: slang for the things that bite and chew in the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: A rule with teeth has the power to be enforced, and choppers is slang for what we bite with.

clue.text: Perceptive wife cleared out grate

indicators.note: the wife letter is cleared out of the word for perceptive

parts.note: a shrewd person is sharp and perceptive

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed woman empties the fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grate' looks like a fireplace noun, but it is the verb, as with cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: To shred food is to cut it into thin strips, much as to grate it.

clue.text: New acid revitalised battery

indicators.note: the letters are given new life in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Fresh acid has recharged a battery.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is short for nickel-cadmium, a rechargeable cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickel-cadmium rechargeable cell is a type of battery.

clue.text: A tyrannical male condemned food processor

indicators.note: something condemned is ruined, so these letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A despotic man is sentenced, the kitchen gadget aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'food processor' looks like the kitchen appliance, but it is the digestive tract.
explanation.definitionFit: The digestive tract from mouth to anus processes what we eat.

clue.text: Showcase clothing in general

indicators.note: the clothing word goes inside the general's name

parts.note: Lord Kitchener was a British field marshal of the First World War
dress means clothing, attire

explanation.surface: A display of clothes worn by a military commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like the containment signal, but it is DRESS; 'in' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen dresser has open shelves on which china is displayed, a kind of showcase.

clue.text: See 23
